title: Aramco and Pasqal Launch Saudi Arabia's First Quantum Computer and Middle East's First Commercial QCaaS Platform
detail: Saudi Aramco and French quantum computing firm Pasqal officially inaugurated Saudi Arabia's first quantum computer at Aramco's Dhahran data center on May 18. The Pasqal Quantum Processing Unit uses neutral-atom technology controlling 200 programmable qubits, making it among the most advanced commercially deployed quantum systems in the region. Simultaneously, the partnership launched the Middle East's first commercial Quantum Computing as a Service (QCaaS) platform, offering cloud-based access to quantum hardware for research and industrial applications. Planned use cases include port and supply chain logistics optimization, CO₂ storage simulations, oil well placement modeling, and drilling rig scheduling — all directly applicable to Aramco's core operations. Aramco's venture capital arm Wa'ed Ventures had invested in Pasqal in January 2023. The launch was timed to align with the Saudi AI investment announcements from Trump's May 13–14 visit, reinforcing Vision 2030's technology diversification agenda.

title: Saudi Supreme Court Declares Start of Dhul-Hijjah 1447 AH — Hajj Season Officially Opens
detail: Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court officially declared May 18, 2026 as the first day of Dhul-Hijjah 1447 AH, setting the Hajj calendar for 2026. Hajj — the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca — is expected to draw over 2.5 million worshippers, placing immense logistical demands on the Kingdom's transport, medical, and security infrastructure. Saudi Health Ministry briefings confirmed medical readiness protocols for the pilgrimage season. The Custodianship of the Two Holy Mosques — one of the Saudi royal family's core legitimizing titles — is managed through the General Presidency for the Affairs of the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque. Mecca's infrastructure projects, including metro expansions and the planned New Mecca Airport, were cited as on track despite broader Vision 2030 budget pressures from the Iran war. The Hajj season represents a critical annual test of Saudi governance capacity and a significant revenue event for the tourism sector.

media.caption: Saudi Supreme Court announces start of Dhul-Hijjah 1447 AH — Hajj 2026 pilgrimage season officially opens
